category_source_basis: Existing R130/I4 evaluation dimensions: dialogue/subtext, character voice differentiation, physicalization, pacing/line economy, ensemble/relationship craft.

Existing R4A axes: character_relationship_integrity, ensemble_downstream_decision_ownership, escalation_pacing, dialogue_subtext_naturalness, stage_direction_playability, broadcast_readiness_non_generic_specificity.
Pre-inspection SYNC-R29 hypotheses: scene-specific dramatic choice, subtext, relationship pressure/status movement, surprise, line intentionality.

frozen_categories.DIALOGUE_SUBTEXT: Preference reason credits implication, avoidance, humor, indirect emotional information, or dialogue carrying more than literal exposition.
frozen_categories.CHARACTER_VOICE: Preference reason credits differentiated/idiosyncratic speech, life-language, occupational voice, or speaker-specific verbal rhythm.
frozen_categories.RELATIONSHIP_STATUS_PRESSURE: Preference reason credits trust, hierarchy, threat, family/work ethical conflict, power relation, status movement, or relational pressure embedded in the scene.
frozen_categories.PHYSICALIZATION_ACTION: Preference reason credits action, prop/object use, blocking, work process, command/action simultaneity, or procedure becoming dramatic action rather than explanation.
frozen_categories.PACING_ESCALATION_TIME_PRESSURE: Preference reason credits compression, countdown, immediacy, scene-goal pressure, rising end pressure, or escalation rhythm.
frozen_categories.ENSEMBLE_WORLD_SPECIFICITY: Preference reason credits multiple characters functioning distinctly, occupational/world specificity, group rhythm, community texture, or ensemble energy.
frozen_categories.INFORMATION_REVEAL_IRREVERSIBILITY: Preference reason credits reversal, disclosure, surprise, trust collapse, irreversible emotional/informational turn, or revelation shock.
frozen_categories.LINE_ECONOMY_RHYTHM: Preference reason credits economy, short-line rhythm, question/avoidance rhythm, compactness, or removal of explanatory verbal overhead.

coding_rule.unit: one sealed Stage-B reason string per BPAIR
coding_rule.primary_label: choose the single category most directly named as the preference basis; ties resolved by earliest explicit craft basis in the reason, not by winner identity
coding_rule.secondary_labels: up to two additional categories only when explicitly supported by wording
coding_rule.unknown_rule: if no frozen category is explicit, label UNCLASSIFIED rather than create a new category
coding_rule.mapping_blind_first_pass: code all 12 reasons before opening the already-sealed historical Stage-B mapping
coding_rule.mapping_use_after_coding: after first-pass labels are sealed, open only the historical I4C Stage-B mapping/result needed to identify whether the preferred side was candidate or human and which selected scene/pair it represents
coding_rule.R4A_mapping: PROHIBITED; current R4A mapping remains closed and unrelated

analysis_outputs: overall frequency of primary/secondary craft bases
candidate-win vs human-win primary/secondary category frequencies after historical unblind
whether human wins cluster in one or more higher-level craft dimensions not captured by the prior deterministic proxy diagnostic
guardrails: no causal claim from one internal judge rationale set
no renderer intervention authorized solely from this exploratory taxonomy
if a stable cluster appears, it may only motivate a fresh blind annotation/replication prereg before prospective intervention
